title: Policy Assistant — live questions with a cited source
story: Each role has a Policy Assistant page. It answers from the policy document library (Handbook, Research Protocol and the Draft Operations Manual; see {case:policy-documents}) and always shows the document and the page or section it used, so an answer can be checked instead of trusted. Staff and administrators can also focus the assistant on one student record; the Dean, Faculty and Student pages answer policy questions only (the student page can also read that student's own record).

In this case the questions are typed live, the way the panel would ask them. The answers below were observed in this run. The assistant is running in its local keyword-search mode: the label under each answer reads **Answered from the documents (keyword search)**, with the note No AI key is set, so answers are quoted straight from the documents. It can therefore quote the right passage with its document, printed page and section, but it does not rephrase it, and a question worded differently can find different passages. Each answer ends with a **Sources** panel that opens to show the document, page, section and the exact passage.
accounts: Policy & Case Guidance chat (can focus on a student)
Student Policy Assistant with manual references
data: Can a student withdraw a subject on Day 1, and how much is the fee?
Is time on leave of absence included in the maximum years to finish a master's degree?
Adding a subject is allowed until when?
Can I file a leave of absence during the last two weeks of the semester?
What is the maximum residence for a master's program?
How many advisees can a faculty member handle in a semester?

parts.title: Part A - Staff: Policy & Case Guidance

steps.text: Sign in as **staff@usls.edu.ph** and open **Policy Assistant** under Monitoring & support. The page is titled **Policy & Case Guidance**. The chat opens with a greeting that says answers come from live records and the policy library and always show the sources. On the right are an optional **Focus on a student** box and **Example questions**, which are shortcuts only: any question can be typed. A **How this works** note says that every answer lists its sources, that opening one shows the document, page, section and exact passage, and that if the documents do not answer a question the assistant says so instead of guessing.

shots.caption: Staff Policy & Case Guidance page: the chat, the optional student focus, and the example questions.

steps.text: Click the question box and type **Can a student withdraw a subject on Day 1, and how much is the fee?** Press Enter. The answer reads: Day 1 is inside the first week, so a student may withdraw a subject on Day 1 with the Dean's approval, but it is not free: 10% of the total amount due for the term is charged in the first week and 20% in the second; a student may also change or add a subject only in the first week; after the second week the student may still withdraw but pays the full fees. Below it are the line **Source: USLS Graduate School Operations Manual (draft for validation) (4.4 Withdrawal of subject)**, the line **Draft - pending Graduate School validation**, the label **Answered from the documents (keyword search)** and a collapsed **Sources (1)** panel.

shots.caption: The Day 1 question: the answer, the Draft warning, and the cited source (Operations Manual, section 4.4).

steps.text: Select the entry in **Sources (1)**. It opens to show a yellow **Draft - pending Graduate School validation** tag, the document and section (4.4 Withdrawal of subject) and the exact passage the answer was taken from, set off with a green rule.

shots.caption: The opened source: document, section and the exact passage, flagged as a Draft.

steps.text: Ask **Is time on leave of absence included in the maximum years to finish a master's degree?** The answer is the Handbook: a master's program must be finished within a maximum of seven (7) academic years including Leave of Absence (LOA), and a student who cannot finish within seven years must re-enroll all courses taken. The source line reads Graduate School Handbook 2022-2023 (p. 54, 3.6 MAXIMUM RESIDENCE - Master's Program), and the Sources panel lists the Handbook, page 54.

shots.caption: Leave and maximum residence: the Handbook passage and the Operations Manual passage, each cited.

steps.text: Ask **Adding a subject is allowed until when?** The answer is the Handbook sentence that adding subjects is allowed during the first week of classes upon the written approval of the Associate Dean. The source line reads Graduate School Handbook 2022-2023 (p. 49, 3.1 REGISTRATION - Adding of Subject/s).

shots.caption: Adding a subject: first week only, cited to the Handbook and the Operations Manual.

parts.title: Part B - Student, Dean and Faculty

steps.text: In a separate session sign in as **student@usls.edu.ph** and open **Policy Assistant** under Support. The **Student Policy Assistant** states that it is private and read-only: it can use approved handbook content and the signed-in student's own record, cannot see other students and cannot change grades, enrollment, requests or records. Suggested questions sit on the right.

shots.caption: Student Policy Assistant: private and read-only, with suggested questions.

steps.text: Type **Can I file a leave of absence during the last two weeks of the semester?** and select **Ask assistant**. The answer quotes the Handbook: no leave of absence shall be granted during the semester within two (2) weeks before the last day of classes, and a student returning from leave declares the intention to enroll in writing. The source line reads Graduate School Handbook 2022-2023 (p. 52, 3.4 ATTENDANCE - Leave of Absence), followed by the same keyword-search label and a **Sources (1)** panel naming the Handbook, page 52.

shots.caption: Student question: the answer with its Manual references (Handbook p. 57 and the Draft Operations Manual).

steps.text: In a separate session sign in as **dean@usls.edu.ph** and open **Policy Assistant** under Monitoring & support. The chat is labelled **Policy documents only**. Type **What is the maximum residence for a master's program?** The answer quotes the Handbook: candidacy within three academic years and all requirements within five, a two-year extension with a graded 6-unit refresher, and a master's program finished within seven academic years including Leave of Absence. The source line reads Graduate School Handbook 2022-2023 (p. 54, 3.6 MAXIMUM RESIDENCE - Master's Program).

shots.caption: Dean: the same assistant, policy documents only, with the Handbook page cited.

steps.text: In a separate session sign in as **liwayway.bautista@usls.edu.ph** and open **Policy Assistant** under Support. Type **How many advisees can a faculty member handle in a semester?** The answer is the Handbook: a maximum of five advisees per semester, and in some cases more where there are fewer faculty in the program. The source line reads Graduate School Handbook 2022-2023 (p. 59, 3.10 PROJECT PAPER, THESIS & DISSERTATION - Project Paper/Thesis/Dissertation Adviser).

shots.caption: Faculty: maximum of five advisees per semester, cited to Handbook p. 63.

parts.title: Part C - What the panel should know about the answers
steps: The assistant retrieves passages by keyword and quotes them; it does not interpret them. Wording matters. In the same run, **Is time on leave of absence included in the maximum years...** found the exact Handbook sentence, while the shorter **Does time on leave of absence count toward the maximum residence?** returned only the open-question line OQ-10 from the Draft Operations Manual. If an answer looks off, rephrase using the words of the policy (leave of absence, maximum, first week, written approval).
Page numbers in the source lines are the printed page numbers of the Handbook, the same pages that the Business Rules register cites (for example, the adding-a-subject rule is on p. 49 in both).

A Draft source is labelled every time it is used. Answers that rest on the Operations Manual say so in the answer text and in the opened source, and the Graduate School is asked to validate that document before it is treated as policy.

notes: Guidance only: the assistant does not approve anything. Final decisions stay with authorized personnel.

The assistant runs in keyword-search mode here (label: Answered from the documents (keyword search); note: No AI key is set). No Gemini key was in use, so no answer was written by an AI model. With a key configured the screen is meant to give fuller, reworded answers; this walkthrough did not run that mode.
The student assistant can also answer from the student's own record (for example, What should I do next based on my record? answers from Miguel Yu's record with no policy citation).

Not every question finds the right passage. In this run the panel-size question (How many members must a thesis defense panel have?) found the Research Protocol Title Defense passage (chair and 2, 3 or 4 members by paper type), but a question outside the library (Who pays for the printing of hard-bound copies?) returned loosely related passages about hard-bound reproduction instead of saying the answer is not in the documents.
